questions_and_answers.question: What type of noun is formed by using the infinitive as a noun in German?
Which suffix is added to a masculine noun to form its feminine counterpart (e.g., Freund → Freundin)?
What suffix replaces -en to form die-words from many infinitives (e.g., wohnen → die Wohnung)?
Which suffix is used to form der-words from infinitives that designate persons?
Which suffixes correspond to English '-ness' or '-ity' when forming nouns from adjectives?
Which suffix forms nouns from nouns and functions like English '-hood' or '-ship'?
Which of the following pairs illustrates the use of the suffix -ung?
Which example shows a noun formed with -er denoting a person?
What is the German noun for 'beauty'?
Which suffix forms feminine nouns like 'Brüderschaft' and 'Botschaft'?

articles.text:
E. DERIVATIVE NOUNS
In German as in English a number of nouns can be formed from other words (verbs, adjectives, other nouns), usually by the addition of a noun-forming suffix. Examples are such words as printing, goodness, friendship, practicality. The process is not indiscriminate or automatic, however, and only certain words lend themselves to it.
1. The simplest formation consists in the use of the infinitive as a noun. The English equivalent may be either a noun or a related noun or in some cases a completely different word. Note that it is always a das-noun. Examples: das Wissen (wissen – knowledge), das Aussehen (aussehen – appearance), das Schreiben (schreiben – writing, official letter), das Essen (essen – food, meal), das Einrichten (einrichten – arranging). Form nouns from the following infinitives and give their English equivalents: gehen, rauchen, können, reinigen, sprechen, treffen, leben, denken.
2. There are a number of examples of a die-word formed from a der-word by the addition of the suffix -in. These words all designate the feminine counterpart of the masculine word. Compare the English suffixes -ess and -rix (actress, aviatrix). Examples: der Gemahl – die Gemahlin (husband – wife), der Sekretär – die Sekretärin (secretary [man] – secretary [woman]), der Freund – die Freundin (friend [man] – friend [woman]), der Amerikaner – die Amerikanerin (American – American [woman]). Form nouns from the following pairs and give their English equivalents.
3. Die-words are formed from many infinitives by substitution of the suffix -ung for the ending -en: besorgen – die Besorgung (errand), wohnen – die Wohnung (apartment), bestellen – die Bestellung (order), ordnen – die Ordnung (order, neatness), stellen – die Stellung (position). Form nouns of this type from the following infinitives and give their English equivalents: stören, verbinden, verzeihen, vorstellen, zahlen, bezahlen.
4. Der-words are formed from many infinitives by substituting the suffix -er for the ending -en. Notice that these nouns all designate persons. A very few words have umlaut of the stem vowel with this suffix. Examples: arbeiten – der Arbeiter (worker), mieten – der Mieter (tenant, lessee), schreiben – der Schreiber (clerk, scribe), verkaufen – der Verkäufer (sales clerk). Form nouns from the following infinitives and give their English equivalents: besuchen, denken, laufen, lesen, fahren, rauchen, finden, trinken, hören, übersetzen, kaufen, vermieten.
5. Die-words are formed from many adjectives by the addition of suffixes -heit or -keit. These suffixes thus work like English -ness, -ity, etc. With suffix -heit: schön – die Schönheit (beauty), rein – die Reinheit (purity), mehr – die Mehrheit (majority). Form nouns from the following adjectives and give their English equivalents: berühmt. With suffix -keit: ähnlich – die Ähnlichkeit (similarity), möglich – die Möglichkeit (possibility), richtig – die Richtigkeit (correctness), bestimmt – die Bestimmtheit, einfach. Form nouns from the following adjectives and give their English equivalents: gemütlich, wahrscheinlich, langsam, wichtig, natürlich, wirklich, sauber, zufällig.
6. Die-words are formed from certain other nouns by the addition of the suffix -schaft. This suffix works like English -hood and -ship. Some words have umlaut of the stem vowel with this suffix, and some nouns lose a final -e. Examples: der Bruder – die Brüderschaft (brotherhood), der Bote – die Botschaft (message, embassy), der Herr – die Herrschaften (ladies and gentlemen), der Ort – die Ortschaft (locality). Form nouns from the following nouns and give their English equivalents: Bekannte, Freund, Nachbar, Vater, Verwandte.
